title: AiProvider
description: A custom AI Firewall provider owned by the tenant: a model server the gateway forwards to, beside the built-in catalogue. Only this tenant sees or uses it. metadata.name is the provider slug, which becomes the gateway path prefix (/<slug>/<org>/v1/...) and is what AiFirewallPolicy providers and models refer to. A tenant has at most 10 custom providers, and a slug that a built-in provider uses is refused at apply.

name.description: The slug: 2 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter. The gateway's own path words and Belai's compiled-in provider names are reserved; a built-in provider's slug is refused at apply.

displayName.description: The label the console shows. Defaults to the slug.

serverKind.description: The server type. ollama and llama-server speak openai-chat only.

protocol.description: The request surface the server speaks: openai-chat (Chat Completions), openai-responses (Responses, which Codex needs) or anthropic-messages (Messages, which Claude Code speaks). The gateway refuses requests on any other surface.

baseUrl.description: https://host[:port] and nothing more: no path, query or fragment. The gateway adds the protocol's own path. The host must be publicly reachable; private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused at apply, and again at every connection.

auth.description: How the API key is sent. bearer: Authorization: Bearer <key>. x-api-key: an x-api-key header, plus anthropic-version for anthropic-messages. cf-aig: a cf-aig-authorization header, for Cloudflare AI Gateway.

apiKey.description: Where the client reads the API key. It is stored encrypted for this tenant and provider, and is never exported or shown in a plan. Left out, the key on the server is kept; with no key at all, the gateway refuses requests with provider_key_missing.

id.description: The model id the server expects, without spaces.
